oracle_note: Every oracle_kappa below is INDEPENDENT, hand-computed ground truth derived from the textbook Cohen's kappa formula by exact rational arithmetic (Python Fraction), NEVER by calling persona's cohens_kappa. Binary kappa: po = fraction of items where the two raters agree; pe = pa*pb + (1-pa)*(1-pb) where pa, pb are each rater's fraction of positives; kappa = (po - pe)/(1 - pe). rater values are 1=endorse, 0=reject. po == raw_agreement; the discriminator case proves kappa != raw_agreement.

cases.derivation: agree on 7/10 -> po=0.70; pa=3/10=0.3, pb=4/10=0.4; pe=0.3*0.4+0.7*0.6=0.54; kappa=(0.70-0.54)/(1-0.54)=8/23=0.3478 -> 0.348. DISCRIMINATOR: both base rates in [0.2,0.8] (in-band), raw_agreement=0.70 >= 0.6 would PASS an agreement-floor gate, but real kappa=0.348 < 0.6 correctly FIRES the gate. Substituting raw-agreement for kappa flips the gate decision.

agree on 8/10 -> po=0.80; pa=5/10=0.5, pb=5/10=0.5; pe=0.5*0.5+0.5*0.5=0.50; kappa=(0.80-0.50)/(1-0.50)=3/5=0.600. At pa=pb=0.5, pe=0.5 -> kappa = 2*po-1; kappa(0.60) != raw(0.80). Sits exactly on the 0.6 floor (boundary check: gate fires only on kappa < floor).
identical raters -> po=1.0; pa=pb=3/5=0.6; pe=0.6*0.6+0.4*0.4=0.52; kappa=(1.0-0.52)/(1-0.52)=1.0. Degenerate +1: perfect agreement beyond chance.
raters never agree -> po=0.0; equal base rates pa=pb=2/4=0.5 so pe=0.5; kappa=(0.0-0.5)/(1-0.5)=-1.0. Degenerate -1: maximal disagreement (requires equal base rates for exactly -1).

agree on 2/4 -> po=0.5; pa=pb=2/4=0.5; pe=0.5*0.5+0.5*0.5=0.5; kappa=(0.5-0.5)/(1-0.5)=0.0. Agreement exactly at chance -> kappa=0 even though raw agreement is 0.50. Pins that the (1-pa)(1-pb) term is present: dropping it gives pe=0.25 and kappa=0.333, not 0.

both raters endorse everything -> pa=pb=1.0; pe=1.0*1.0+0.0*0.0=1.0; kappa=(po-pe)/(1-pe) is 0/0 -> undefined. persona returns float('nan') when p_e == 1. Out-of-band (rates not in [0.2,0.8]), so this never gates regardless.
len(a) != len(b) -> kappa undefined by construction. persona returns float('nan') for the n==0 or n!=len(b) guard. Oracle is NaN by definition, not from arithmetic.
